subject: SecureLogix S3 incident — request for IR artifacts and SOC 2 evidence
messages:
From: James Holt <j.holt@securelogix.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: securelogix-security@securelogix.com, priya.singh@legal-sec.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Potential S3 exposure — initial alert and request

Hi Mateo,

We detected a short-lived presigned URL pattern in one of your customer-facing buckets that matched traffic from our regular scans. At this point we can't confirm data exfiltration, but the request distribution looks unusual and we want to notify you and request the following to accelerate triage:

- Short-term access logs for the affected bucket (UTC 2026-07-13 22:00 -> 2026-07-14 08:00)
- List of active pre-signed URLs issued in the past 48 hours (with issuing principal)
- Any active IAM policies or roles bound to the bucket with write permissions

We're happy to coordinate an emergency call. Please also provide a primary point of contact for incident handling and your IR plan summary. I've attached the sample log snippet we observed for your reference (presigned-url-dump.txt).

Thanks,
James Holt
Security Operations
SecureLogix

Attachment: presigned-url-dump.txt (text)
From: mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
To: James Holt <j.holt@securelogix.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwoodinference.com, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential S3 exposure — initial alert and request

Hi James — thanks for the heads up and the sample. We've opened an internal incident and I'll be the primary contact for SecureLogix while we triage. Initial answers below and next steps: 

- I'll export the bucket access logs you requested and attach the CSV in the follow-up (we're pulling the range you specified).
- We rotate presigned URL tooling on a short cadence; I'll collect issuance metadata and the principals tied to any URLs in the last 48 hours.
- IAM write bindings: none of our service roles should have public write access; still validating a recent rollout to a beta worker pool.

Planned next steps (ETA in hours):
1) 10:00 PDT: Security sync (Monica leading) — scope confirms whether this is false positive or sign of misuse.
2) 13:00 PDT: Share sanitized access log extract + issuance list.
3) 15:00 PDT: Joint call with SecureLogix if needed.

Cc'ing Monica (security ops) and Neha (compliance) — Monica will circulate the IRP summary and artifacts we can share under our SOC 2 NDA. If you need faster access, let us know and we'll expedite a secure transfer.

— Mateo Alvarez
Sr. Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
To: James Holt <j.holt@securelogix.com>, mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 12:58:00 -07:00
Subject: IR artifacts: logs and SOC 2 evidence path

Hi James / team — following the sync, attaching the initial artifacts we can provide under the existing SCP/NDA. Summary below; full exports are in the shared Drive link.

What we're sharing (sanitized):
- s3_access_audit_2026-07-14.csv — consolidated request logs (requester IPs hashed, timestamps, operation types).
- irp_summary_redwood_v1.pdf — executive IR plan highlights: notification flow, escalation matrix, retention windows, and evidence preservation steps.

Notes and constraints:
- The CSV has hashed IPs per our data retention and privacy commitments; we can provide mapping for legal requests only.
- SOC 2 artifacts (control evidence) are listed in the Drive folder under /SOC2/Evidence-Request/ — see link below. If SecureLogix needs the SIG or CAIQ-specific crosswalk, we can produce a redacted bundle; that takes ~48 hours to compile.

Suggested immediate next actions:
1) Secure transfer of the full logs if you confirm your S3 findings indicate active exfiltration (we're prepared to enable a signed, time-limited share).
2) Joint forensic call at 15:00 PDT — Mateo and I will be on the line.
3) If legal escalation is requested, loop in our counsel (Aditya Rao).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_securelogix_ir
Jira: JIRA-SUP-9821
HubSpot: HS-123456

Attachments: s3_access_audit_2026-07-14.csv, irp_summary_redwood_v1.pdf

Regards,
Monica Patel
Manager, Security Operations
Redwood Inference
From: James Holt <j.holt@securelogix.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwoodinference.com, priya.singh@legal-sec.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SecureLogix S3 incident — request for IR artifacts and SOC 2 evidence

Mateo / Monica — thank you for the fast turnaround and the artifacts. The CSV shows three requester patterns we want to review further; we'll prepare our initial triage notes and raise any subpoenas through the legal channel if we confirm unauthorized downloads.

We accept the proposed 15:00 PDT forensic call — Priya from our legal team will join. Please confirm dial-in and whether you prefer a screened Google Meet or encrypted bridge. Also, if you can flag any entries in the CSV that look like large GET ranges, that will speed our mutual review.

Appreciate the partnership — we'll aim to keep this coordinated through JIRA-SUP-9821.

Best,
James Holt
Security Operations
SecureLogix
